column1: # Which repo path each template owns, and how strictly it is compared.
# comparison
#   identical  byte-for-byte. The strictness is the point: a missing trailing
#              newline is drift, and it is the half of this class that no diff
#              view shows.
#   contains   every non-blank, non-comment line of the template appears in the
#              target. Repos legitimately add entries of their own to these
#              files; they may not drop the shared ones.
#   suffix     the template's non-blank, non-comment lines must be the
#              target's own final such lines, in order. Only CODEOWNERS needs
#              this: GitHub applies the last matching pattern, so position is
#              the whole mechanism, not just presence.
# mypy.ini stays on `contains`, not `suffix`, despite carrying the same kind
# of risk CODEOWNERS does — a real mypy 1.19.0 run (docs/shell-and-python.md)
# showed that a second `[mypy]` header makes mypy silently drop every setting
# in the file, in EITHER position, not just a later one; `suffix` would
# therefore give no real protection while also blocking the one place a repo
# needs to add its own line (`python_version`, inside the same section, never
# a new header). `tools/ts/src/pythonConfigGate.ts`'s PythonConfigGate is
# what actually catches a duplicate `[mypy]` header, mechanically.
# A template file that is not listed here is a hard error, not a finding — an
# unregistered template is enforced by nothing and says so nowhere.
